body:
Don't take the following at face-value. Check it, and recommend how solace should be amended to address these shortcomings.

`submit --imports` is documented as replacing a module's imports and module comment, but it also requires the header to keep the module's `mod x;` list. In run 86faf39d0c8095d6 on task:9c5dd4d28f6b4ef3, the worker sent only `use` lines; the `fsx` header's `mod tests;` was missing. `submit_imports_rust` compared the `mod` lists, found them different, and refused with "`--imports` can't add or remove a module". The worker tried with and without the module comment, then replaced the whole `fsx` module to add `std::thread` and `std::time::{Duration, Instant}`. The `read` refusal also sent it to `view fsx --bodies` (85 KB) instead of `view fsx --header`, which shows exactly the header `--imports` needs.

Done when:
- `submit --imports <module>` accepts a header with the module comment, imports and the same `mod` list; a test covers adding `use std::time::{Duration, Instant};` to `fsx`.
- When the `mod` list differs or is missing, the error says the header must keep it and names `view <module> --header`; a test covers the message.
- The `read` refusal for a symbol-held source names `view <module> --header` for the header, not just `--bodies`; a test covers it.
- `submit` still auto-adds a standard-library import when there is exactly one match, and the multi-match refusal lists the choices.
title: submit: add imports without replacing a module
